newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra confirms Telstra employee share plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra confirms Telstra employee share plan.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard confirmed on Thursday the government's plan to offer special deals for Telstra Corp employees when one-third of the telecoms carrier was sold.
"The workers involved in Telstra will get a special deal in the public float," Howard told Parliament.
Howard said the government would reserve two percent of the one-third of Telstra to be sold for the company's employees.

"Under a generous employee share ownership plan, a special offer of one free share for every four shares purchased will be made to Telstra employees with a maximum of 500 free shares for each employee," he said.
In addition, loyalty bonuses would be available to Telstra employees who held their shares in Telstra for at least 12 months, he said.
"Telstra has already been made fully aware of this employee share ownership plan, which was announced by the (Liberal-National) coalition before the election and which I confirm today," he said.
The upper house of parliament, the Senate, approved late on Wednesday the government's plan to sell one-third of Telstra for about A$8.0 billion.
Telecommunication analysts have said the sale was most likely to take place in the final quarter of calendar 1997.
